reviewer: Claude Code (AI first-pass source audit; not an independent human curator)
scope: 1-based manifest positions 151-160 of data/validation/self_run_p0_candidates.json, frozen order; 10 candidates, 12 arms
blinding: self_run_p0_predictions.json and all model outputs were NOT opened. The FRDB snapshot /tmp/sisyphus-frdb-v2024-12-30.zip (SHA256 647b80d9...9c7a, verified) was read with every column containing 'cmax' dropped before any row was printed. Arms were mapped by dose, AUC, t1/2, n, sex, population comments and application comments only. Original-source Cmax values were then read from original tables, registry results or abstracts. The sunepitron abstract prints EM/PM Cmax next to phenotype labels, so mapping there is by FRDB population comment. The clonixin abstract prints reference Cmax next to t1/2, so mapping there is by t1/2 1.3 h. No observed-vs-predicted comparison was made.
method_note: Single AI pass. Full originals read: PMC6304249 (berberine; Europe PMC XML incl. Table 6), IJPPS acotiamide open-access PDF (via headless browser; curl got Cloudflare 403), PMDA Acofide review report 000153467.pdf, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 record NCT02959138 with results, and the University of Groningen oxyphenonium thesis summary (manifest core.ac.uk /download/pdf/ path 404; alternate /download/ path served the same record's PDF). Closed originals were time-boxed to abstracts or landing pages: Springer (nifuratel), Taylor & Francis Bioanalysis (ornidazole), Dustri (clonixin), Wiley J Clin Pharmacol (ranirestat), DMD/Elsevier (sunepitron). Baicalin was judged from its abstract (ineligible). Only PubMed E-utilities (via MCP), Europe PMC REST, ClinicalTrials.gov API, publisher pages, CORE and PMDA were queried. No email, contact identifier or Unpaywall was used. Transient headless-browser files that this pass created in the gitignored .playwright-mcp/ were deleted; no repository file was modified.
unresolved_issues: Berberine (1933): verified_with_caveat. The value is Table 6 of an open DDI paper (overnight fast, 3 x 100 mg berberine chloride tablets, parent plasma). Caveats: salt-basis dose, group n not printed, duplicated AUC values across rows (a data-quality flag), and a low-concentration Cmax.

Acotiamide (8241): frdb_8115 is verified_with_caveat (IJPPS Table 6 reference arm, overnight fast). The Results text swaps the test/reference labels, the variability is implausibly low, and the dose is on the HCl-hydrate basis. frdb_8116 is ineligible: the PMDA MAD study dosed before a meal, which PMDA itself shows raises Cmax by 63% vs fasted.

Oxyphenonium (2569): ineligible. The source is a 1981 thesis summary; the subjects were CARA (chronic respiratory disease) patients, and the value is approximate ('about 5 ng/ml'). The manifest URI is 404; the same CORE record resolves at core.ac.uk/download/232467634.pdf.
Baicalin (22343): ineligible. The dosed drug is baicalein chewable tablets; baicalin is its metabolite.

Clonixin (3177): unverified. Reference Cmax 32.39 µg/mL (fasting, IR tablets) is in the abstract, but the matrix is unstated and the full text is paywalled. The manifest dose of 250 mg is lysine clonixinate (≈160.6 mg clonixin acid); this 1.56x salt-basis discrepancy must be resolved before scoring.

Lanraplenib (59604): unverified. The CT.gov healthy-control Cmax (131.6 ng/mL, fasted, tablets) is mapped cleanly, but the registry does not name the matrix, and the controls are older subjects matched to renal-impairment patients.
Sunepitron (2804): both arms unverified. EM/PM Cmax values (1.02/10.92 ng/mL) come from the abstract; fasting and dosage form are in the paywalled DMD full text. The PM arm is n=2.

Nifuratel (5563), ornidazole (3430), ranirestat (8213): unverified. The originals are paywalled and their abstracts give no Cmax. Ranirestat's arm is the normal-hepatic-function control group of an impairment study.

arms.reason: Mapped by AUC0-inf 6.28 μg·h/L and t1/2 30.6 h, which match the 'Bbr' (berberine alone) single-dose row of Table 6; FRDB n=60 is total trial enrollment across 5 parallel groups, not the Bbr-alone group size. Parent berberine plasma Cmax read from Table 6. Caveats: dose is 300 mg of berberine chloride (salt basis; ~271 mg cation) given as 3 x 100 mg conventional tablets (IR not explicitly stated); the Bbr-alone group size is not printed in the accessible text (~12 by 60/5); the table shows identical AUC values for Bbr and Bbr(Svt) rows and implausible Cl values, a data-quality flag; Cmax is near the 0.05 ng/mL LLOQ region with high CV (73%).

arms.reason: The accessible source is the English summary of a 1981 Groningen PhD thesis (Greving). Oral PK was studied after 10 mg oxyphenonium bromide (2 Antrenyl tablets) in patients with CARA (chronic aspecific respiratory affections; COPD/asthma) studied 'under standardized conditions', not healthy adults. The summary gives only 'about 5 ng/ml' (no statistic) from means of estimates in 7 patients; fasting is not stated; dose is on the bromide-salt basis.

arms.reason: Abstract gives reference-product (Dorixina Forte) Cmax 32.39 ± 8.32 µg/mL with t1/2 1.3 h, matching FRDB t1/2 1.3 h; FRDB AUC0-inf 49.88 is not printed in the abstract (abstract AUC0-8h 48.92), so the reference-arm mapping is probable but not table-confirmed. arms.reason: Mapped by AUClast 537.2 and t1/2 8.99, which match the 300 mg Day 1 row of Table 23 (Japanese phase I multiple-dose study). Dosing in this study was 'before a meal' (preprandial), not fasted. The same PMDA report (Tables 20-21) shows preprandial dosing raises Cmax by 62.7% vs fasted (GMR 1.627 [1.380, 1.918]), so the FRDB FASTED tag is wrong for this arm. Day 1 is a single dose before a washout and a TID phase; n=6 per dose (FRDB 18 = total enrollment).

notes: Berberine and acotiamide each have a source-mapped numeric parent plasma Cmax but material study-data or salt-basis caveats; neither is promoted to fully verified at this stage.
Acotiamide frdb_8116 is explicitly preprandial in the PMDA source and is ineligible under the same meal-timing rule used for prior batches.
Lanraplenib remains unverified because the registry does not name the sampled matrix; do not assume plasma from a concentration outcome label.
